This is the first role of its kind at Harvey — and one of the highest-leverage seats in the company. The Marketing Engineer sits at the exact point where growth strategy meets world-class AI execution: you'll take the ideas marketing bets on and turn them into shipped, compounding systems.

You'll partner directly with marketing leadership, demand gen, digital marketing, brand, product marketing, and marketing operations to spot the highest-leverage AI opportunities and ship them. Owning everything from the automation running behind the scenes to the experiments running live on harvey.ai. It's a rare opportunity to sit at the intersection of engineering and marketing at a category-defining legal AI company.

What You'll Do

  • Own the identification, scoping, and implementation of AI and automation use cases that improve demand generation velocity, campaign operations, pipeline conversion and more.

  • Build and maintain AI workflows from automated content creation to intelligent audience targeting and personalization at scale.

  • Design and deploy automation workflows (e.g., Claude, Clay, n8n, or equivalent) that eliminate manual work across the demand gen stack, integrating with Marketo, Salesforce, web CMS, and digital platforms.

  • Build and run experimentation infrastructure: A/B tests, landing pages, and conversion-flow changes, directly on harvey.ai and campaign surfaces, not just backend automation.

  • Manage the cost and efficiency of automated workflows.

  • Collaborate with Marketing Operations, Content, and Performance Marketing to translate strategic marketing needs into technical solutions.

  • Continuously evaluate emerging AI capabilities, including new models, agent frameworks, and MCP integrations, and prototype applications that give Harvey's marketing team a competitive edge.

What You Have

  • 4+ years of experience in growth engineering, marketing engineering, GTM engineering, or a technical role within a marketing/growth function at a B2B SaaS company.

  • Hands-on experience building with AI — you use tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent as part of your daily workflow, not just as something you build on top of.

  • Experience working with LLM APIs or AI-powered tools to generate content, automate workflows, or optimize marketing performance.

  • Familiarity with marketing automation platforms (e.g., Marketo, HubSpot), CRMs (e.g., Salesforce), workflow/automation tools (e.g., Clay, n8n, Zapier, Make), and analytics/experimentation tooling (e.g., Amplitude, Mixpanel, Segment, PostHog, GA4).

  • A builder mentality, comfortable operating in ambiguity, shipping iteratively, and taking ownership of 0→1 projects.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to design experiments, own attribution, and translate data into decisions.

  • Cross-functional collaboration: work closely with internal teams across data science, marketing operations, performance marketing, product marketing, and sales to ensure campaign success. Drive alignment on priorities and share insights to refine strategies.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with data warehouses/BI tools

  • Strong programming skills

  • Experience building on a marketing site or product surface (landing pages, onboarding, referral or lifecycle systems).

  • Background at a high-growth B2B SaaS or AI-native company.

The Business Development team at Harvey is responsible for enabling step-change outcomes, working in lock-step with sales and product leadership. We rapidly adapt to the changing market environment, unlock new product experiences, and deliver new business. As a member of this team, you will help us build differentiated product offerings and scalable go-to-market motions.

This role involves quarterbacking high-visibility, cross-functional initiatives from idea through execution. You will communicate proactively to meet the needs of our internal and external stakeholders, evaluating potential partnerships, negotiating agreements, and overseeing the integration of partner capabilities into Harvey’s offerings. You will work closely with senior stakeholders across product, finance, legal, and go-to-market functions to drive strategic initiatives and ensure successful partnership outcomes.

Your ability to articulate the value of Harvey's product and sales strategy, coupled with your passion for groundbreaking AI technologies, will help us shape the future of knowledge work.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and execute a strategic plan for partner pursuits, aligned with Harvey’s overall product and GTM strategy.

  • Independently identify, evaluate, and establish a range of partnerships to enhance product functionality and GTM motions.

  • Negotiate complex partnership agreements, ensuring mutually beneficial terms and alignment with company goals.

  • Conduct quantitative analysis, create business cases, and present them to executives.

  • Collaborate closely with product, finance, legal and GTM teams to oversee the successful integration of new partners.

  • Build and nurture strong long-term relationships with key partners, ensuring mutual success and achievement of partnership goals and business objectives.

  • Operate autonomously, being both a proactive executor and strategic thinker.

What You Have

  • 5+ years of experience in business development, product, or corporate development. Experience working at the early stage at a high-growth company, where programs are in their infancy and the partner motion is building.

  • Proven ability to develop executive relationships, negotiate complex contracts, and problem-solve with external partners to drive distribution in new markets.

  • Experience collaborating with product teams to develop and distribute new technology solutions.

  • Team player who can collaborate effectively across internal functions (Product, Legal, GTM, etc.) to achieve common goals.

  • Demonstrated passion for Harvey’s mission and a strong understanding of AI and its potential applications in knowledge work.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills—can influence without authority and drive urgency with empathy.

OTE 70/30 Split $200,000-260,000 USD

Role Overview

Harvey is redefining what an AI-native marketing organization looks like, and this role designs the operating system behind it. The Head of Marketing Operations and Analytics owns the platforms, data, and automation that power Harvey's marketing engine. It's a rare shot at architecting a category-defining function with a brilliant team, an AI-native mandate, and full latitude to build it right for the long term.

You'll build the measurement frameworks, technology stack, and reporting systems that connect every marketing dollar to pipeline and revenue, partnering closely with revenue operations, GTM systems, product marketing, and sales leadership to make Harvey's systems and operations data-driven, compliant, and efficient.

This role will report directly to our Head of Demand Generation, working closely across our entire marketing team.

What You'll Do

  • Own the marketing technology stack — evaluate, implement, and optimize tools across marketing automation, CRM, ad platforms, attribution, lead routing and enrichment, and data visualization to support a modern, AI-first operating model.

  • Lead AI and automation adoption — identify and ship agentic workflows and automation that remove manual work across the funnel; go beyond piloting tools to running them in production.

  • Build unified marketing analytics and reporting — attribution models, pipeline dashboards, and campaign ROI measurement that serve as a single source of truth for marketing, finance, and sales leadership, and translate into clear, actionable insight.

  • Architect lead lifecycle infrastructure — define funnel stages, scoring models, routing logic, and handoff criteria in partnership with revenue operations and sales development.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey’s products all depend on a shared AI foundation: the model layer and agent infrastructure that determine the quality of work our agents deliver. Legal is one of the hardest domains for AI: documents run to hundreds of pages, matters can span millions of files, and there is zero margin for error on accuracy.

The AI Platform team builds the foundation that every product and agent team at Harvey builds upon. This team is early and there’s a lot to build: model routing, agent architecture, context management, evals. Your work here sets the ceiling for what Harvey’s AI can do.

Representative Projects

  • Context Engineering & Agent Infrastructure. Build the platform-level systems for context management, session state, and memory that all of Harvey’s agents and products rely on.

  • Model Integration & Routing. Own the infrastructure that lets Harvey onboard new foundation models fast and route to the right one for every task - a capability every product team depends on.

  • Evaluation Infrastructure. Build the shared eval tooling and frameworks that let every team across Harvey measure and improve AI quality systematically.

  • Shared Abstractions. Create the SDKs, platform primitives, and developer tooling that make it dramatically easier for product teams to ship AI-powered features.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build abstractions and platform-level systems that improve all of Harvey’s agentic products.

  • Own infrastructure for model integration, routing, and evaluation that helps Harvey choose and deploy the right foundation model for any given context.

  • Build evaluation frameworks and tooling that let every team across Harvey iterate on AI quality effectively.

  • Partner closely with product engineering teams, PMs, and design to launch cutting-edge AI products.

  • Evaluate, prototype, and integrate the latest advancements in AI and agentic systems as they emerge.

What You Have

  • 5+ years of experience building backend systems, with at least 1+ year focused on AI/ML engineering. Staff candidates will typically have 8+ years and a track record of technical leadership across teams.

  • Experience building and shipping multi-model or multi-provider AI systems in production.

  • Familiarity with context management, session state, or memory systems in AI or distributed systems. You’ve thought about what the model sees and why it matters.

  • A track record of building internal platforms, SDKs, or shared infrastructure that other engineering teams actually adopted - and an understanding of why developer experience matters as much as raw capability.

  • Strong judgment about abstractions. Opinionated about good design but pragmatic about shipping incrementally.

  • Excitement about agentic AI and the infrastructure challenges of making autonomous systems reliable when the stakes are real.

  • A bias toward full ownership: you navigate ambiguity well and don’t wait for a roadmap to start solving problems.

  • Bonus: experience building evaluation frameworks, working with agent/function-calling architectures, familiarity with legal or other high-stakes professional services domains, or time at early-stage or hyper-growth startups where the underlying technology changes regularly.

Compensation

$193,400 - $290,000 USD

ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey’s products all depend on a shared AI foundation: the model layer and agent infrastructure that determine the quality of work our agents deliver. Legal is one of the hardest domains for AI: documents run to hundreds of pages, matters can span millions of files, and there is zero margin for error on accuracy.

The AI Platform team builds the foundation that every product and agent team at Harvey builds upon. This team is early and there’s a lot to build: model routing, agent architecture, context management, evals. Your work here sets the ceiling for what Harvey’s AI can do.




REPRESENTATIVE PROJECTS

 - Context Engineering & Agent Infrastructure. Build the platform-level systems for context management, session state, and memory that all of Harvey’s agents and products rely on.

 - Model Integration & Routing. Own the infrastructure that lets Harvey onboard new foundation models fast and route to the right one for every task - a capability every product team depends on.

 - Evaluation Infrastructure. Build the shared eval tooling and frameworks that let every team across Harvey measure and improve AI quality systematically.

 - Shared Abstractions. Create the SDKs, platform primitives, and developer tooling that make it dramatically easier for product teams to ship AI-powered features.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Design and build abstractions and platform-level systems that improve all of Harvey’s agentic products.

 - Own infrastructure for model integration, routing, and evaluation that helps Harvey choose and deploy the right foundation model for any given context.

 - Build evaluation frameworks and tooling that let every team across Harvey iterate on AI quality effectively.

 - Partner closely with product engineering teams, PMs, and design to launch cutting-edge AI products.

 - Evaluate, prototype, and integrate the latest advancements in AI and agentic systems as they emerge.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 8+ years of experience building backend systems, with at least 1+ year focused on AI/ML engineering and a track record of technical leadership across teams.

 - Experience building and shipping multi-model or multi-provider AI systems in production.

 - Familiarity with context management, session state, or memory systems in AI or distributed systems. You’ve thought about what the model sees and why it matters.

 - A track record of building internal platforms, SDKs, or shared infrastructure that other engineering teams actually adopted - and an understanding of why developer experience matters as much as raw capability.

 - Strong judgment about abstractions. Opinionated about good design but pragmatic about shipping incrementally.

 - Excitement about agentic AI and the infrastructure challenges of making autonomous systems reliable when the stakes are real.

 - A bias toward full ownership: you navigate ambiguity well and don’t wait for a roadmap to start solving problems.

 - Bonus: experience building evaluation frameworks, working with agent/function-calling architectures, familiarity with legal or other high-stakes professional services domains, or time at early-stage or hyper-growth startups where the underlying technology changes regularly.

As a Software Engineer, Agents, you'll build the systems that make our AI agents indispensable to legal professionals.

You will design environments and actions for agentic professional work, make model selection decisions, manage context windows, create optimal tools, and develop evals that enable faster iteration loops to unlock new capabilities.

We're looking for engineers and researchers who are immersed in the space, driven to ship impactful products, and are experienced in using practical evaluations to drive task completion quality and customer delight.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with customers and PMs to understand legal workflows, design practical evaluations that capture what “excellent” means, and ship agents that get the job done.

  • Optimize agent performance through prompt engineering, model selection, tool design, skill writing, context window management, and eval harness development.

  • Work with our model infra team to design and implement infrastructure for low-latency agent execution, including caching strategies, parallel tool calls, or subagent patterns.

  • Improve our observability and instrumentation to profile agent behavior, identify bottlenecks, and drive optimization decisions.

  • Stay current on new developments in agentic systems and bring those learnings back to the products we build.

What You Have

  • Passion for building effective domain-specific agents.

  • Iterative mindset: you develop proof of concepts, make decisions quickly, and ship v0s.

  • Comfortable with when and how to use evaluations to drive quality.

  • Humble and adaptable about code and frameworks. We expect you to drive adoption of new best practices as they develop.

  • 5-8 years (post-BS/MS) of software engineering experience.

  • We are hiring for this role across Mid, Senior, and Staff levels.

  • Proficiency in Python and experience working with LLM APIs and agent frameworks.

  • Experience with shipping user-facing products, either on the backend or full-stack.

Compensation

$231,000 - $340,000 USD

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As the Engineering Manager for Model Infrastructure, you'll lead the team responsible for the platform powering every model request across Harvey. You'll partner closely with AI Research, Product Engineering, Infrastructure, and external AI providers to ensure our platform remains reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient as our business grows.

Model Infrastructure is one of Harvey's most strategic engineering organizations. Every product capability—from chat experiences and agents to document workflows and future reasoning systems—depends on this platform.

Over the next several years, the team will evolve beyond operating third-party models to building the infrastructure that enables Harvey to train, evaluate, deploy, and operate our own frontier AI models. This role offers the opportunity to shape the technical foundation of Harvey's AI platform and build an organization that will power the company's next phase of growth.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and grow a high-performing team of software engineers responsible for Harvey's Model Infrastructure platform.

  • Define the technical roadmap for model reliability, scalability, and operational excellence.

  • Build highly reliable systems for model provisioning, capacity management, failover, and incident response across multiple AI providers.

  • Own Harvey's multi-provider model platform, including provider integrations, SDK upgrades, API migrations, and onboarding new model providers.

  • Drive the evolution of our Unified Model Controller (UMC) and Model Selector platform to automatically detect degraded models and intelligently route traffic based on health, latency, quality, compliance, and cost.

  • Improve observability through health dashboards, alerting, token usage analytics, cost reporting, and end-to-end model telemetry.

  • Partner with Product Engineering to support new model launches, capacity planning, experimentation, and proactive production monitoring.

  • Lead initiatives to improve inference efficiency, reduce infrastructure costs, and increase model utilization across providers.

  • Build the infrastructure foundation for Harvey's future model training efforts, including data pipelines, model operations, training environments, and AI platform capabilities.

  • Partner with executive leadership on long-term AI infrastructure strategy and vendor relationships.

  • Recruit, mentor, and develop exceptional engineering talent while fostering a culture of technical excellence and operational ownership.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, including multiple years managing high-performing engineering teams.

  • Experience leading teams responsible for large-scale distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong technical background that enables you to guide architectural decisions and mentor senior engineers.

  • Experience operating highly available production services with strong reliability and operational excellence.

  • Experience building platforms that require scalability, observability, automation, and cost optimization.

  • Strong cross-functional leadership skills with the ability to partner effectively across Engineering, Research, Product, and external vendors.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence technical strategy across organizations.

  • A passion for building teams and developing engineering talent.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with AI infrastructure, LLM serving, or machine learning platforms.

  • Experience working with multiple model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, Fireworks, Baseten, or open-source model ecosystems.

  • Experience building inference platforms, model gateways, traffic routing systems, or policy-based serving infrastructure.

  • Experience with Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, and large-scale observability platforms.

  • Experience supporting GPU infrastructure, model training platforms, or ML infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with data platforms and technologies such as Spark, Kafka, Flink, Airflow, or Iceberg.

  • Experience leading organizations through periods of rapid growth and technical transformation.

Compensation

$260,000 - $340,000 USD

Model Infrastructure is one of Harvey's most strategic engineering organizations. Every product capability—from chat experiences and agents to document workflows and future reasoning systems—depends on this platform.

Over the next several years, the team will evolve beyond operating third-party models to building the infrastructure that enables Harvey to train, evaluate, deploy, and operate our own frontier AI models. This role offers the opportunity to shape the technical foundation of Harvey's AI platform and build an organization that will power the company's next phase of growth.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and grow a high-performing team of software engineers responsible for Harvey's Model Infrastructure platform.

 - Define the technical roadmap for model reliability, scalability, and operational excellence.

 - Build highly reliable systems for model provisioning, capacity management, failover, and incident response across multiple AI providers.

 - Own Harvey's multi-provider model platform, including provider integrations, SDK upgrades, API migrations, and onboarding new model providers.

 - Drive the evolution of our Unified Model Controller (UMC) and Model Selector platform to automatically detect degraded models and intelligently route traffic based on health, latency, quality, compliance, and cost.

 - Improve observability through health dashboards, alerting, token usage analytics, cost reporting, and end-to-end model telemetry.

 - Partner with Product Engineering to support new model launches, capacity planning, experimentation, and proactive production monitoring.

 - Lead initiatives to improve inference efficiency, reduce infrastructure costs, and increase model utilization across providers.

 - Build the infrastructure foundation for Harvey's future model training efforts, including data pipelines, model operations, training environments, and AI platform capabilities.

 - Partner with executive leadership on long-term AI infrastructure strategy and vendor relationships.

 - Recruit, mentor, and develop exceptional engineering talent while fostering a culture of technical excellence and operational ownership.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 8+ years of software engineering experience, including multiple years managing high-performing engineering teams.

 - Experience leading teams responsible for large-scale distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

 - Strong technical background that enables you to guide architectural decisions and mentor senior engineers.

 - Experience operating highly available production services with strong reliability and operational excellence.

 - Experience building platforms that require scalability, observability, automation, and cost optimization.

jobs.title: Senior or Staff User Researcher
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is building the future of AI for legal professionals, and understanding our users is core to how we do that. We are looking for a seasoned strategic User Researcher to to join our research function. You are a senior individual contributor who drives high-impact research across multiple teams or a major product area. You move beyond single studies to shape problem definition, influence roadmaps, and elevate research quality through strong craft and partnership. You are comfortable with AI technologies and excited to build research and insight tooling to accelerate our workflows.

Success looks like teams meaningfully change direction based on your insights and influencing roadmap, research quality improves in the teams you support, and you are trusted as a strategic partner and moves at speed, where Harvey builds shared conviction around user truths.

This role directly reports to the Head of User Research and focuses on accelerating the quality and speed at which Harvey ships user-centered AI products. You have the opportunity to co-create tooling or identify the right capabilities to strengthen our research practice. You'll partner closely with research and design leadership, cross-functional stakeholders that keep research and insights running at peak efficiency.

It's a rare opportunity to shape how a category-defining AI company shapes its products from the ground up.

What You'll Do

Lead Complex Research Programs

  • Own research strategy for a product area or cross-team initiative

  • Design and execute end-to-end qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods research

  • Identify patterns across studies and connect insights to product decisions

  • Research how legal professionals work with Harvey and outside of the platform. Translate that into product and design recommendations.

Shape Product Thinking

  • Partner closely with Product Managers and Designers to frame the right problems

  • Influence roadmaps by surfacing unmet user needs, risks, and opportunities

  • Push teams beyond validation toward deeper discovery

  • Develop strong legal domain expertise and excited to become an expert in both the Harvey product and the legal industry

Raise the Bar on Craft

  • Produce clear, compelling synthesis and storytelling

  • Identify where AI reduces friction in research process and comfortable building custom scripts, integrations, or AI agents where off-the-shelf tools fall short

  • Model strong research rigor, ethics, and judgment

  • Ability to prototype and ship research insight tooling improvements yourself before pulling in Eng support

Operate as a Trusted Partner

  • Bring rigor to ambiguous, fast-moving problem spaces where the underlying technology (and user expectations of it) shift quickly

  • Influence without authority across teams

  • Help partners develop stronger research instincts

What You Have

  • 5+ years of user research experience of digital products in fast-paced, high-growth or technically complex environments

  • Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Human-Computer Interaction, Human Factors, Cognitive Science, or a related field required. Advanced degree preferred

  • Track record or portfolio of portfolio-level impact. Experience conducting and defining user research methodologies, integrating qualitative and quantitative insights into design and product strategy.

  • Demonstrated ability to navigate and simplify multifaceted, ambiguous problem spaces while maintaining a high bar for execution.

  • Exceptional storytelling and communication skills—capable of influencing cross-functional partners and aligning diverse perspectives.

  • Experience building or customizing internal tooling (Zapier workflows, Claude skills, Notion workflows, and custom GPTs or research agents) to support insight acceleration.

  • Strong design and product judgment and business acumen. Ability to engage deeply in design critiques and dedicated product area roadmap reviews to contribute insights into planning.

  • A collaborative, low-ego approach that helps teams move quickly, thoughtfully, and inclusively

  • Experience researching AI-powered technology products, and understand how to assess experiences and quality of conversational products.

Compensation

$158,500 - $264,500

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role  Overview

As a Mid Market Account Executive at Harvey, you will drive the growth and success of our AI solutions within the legal and professional services markets. You will be responsible for establishing and growing relationships with mid-sized law firms and corporate and financial services clients, understanding their unique challenges, and presenting AI solutions that streamline their processes and boost productivity. Your ability to articulate the value of Harvey's products, coupled with your passion for groundbreaking AI technologies, will help us shape the future of knowledge work.

What You'll Do

  • Own your book of business by managing a named account list, prioritizing and cultivating inbound leads, and outbounding directly to high-potential prospects.

  • Manage the full customer lifecycle from prospecting to contracting, onboarding, growing, and renewals.

  • Achieve and exceed revenue targets and other key sales metrics.

  • Build strong relationships with key decision-makers and stakeholders, understanding their pain points and aligning Harvey's solutions with their needs.

  • Conduct high velocity, tailored client evaluations, including product demonstrations and presentations, showcasing the power of Harvey's AI systems to prospects and clients.

  • Effectively work cross-functionally across the organization to shape Harvey’s solutions to meet customer needs. Collaborate closely with the engineering and product teams to stay updated on the latest AI advancements and tailor solutions to meet client goals.

  • Develop our sales playbook to enable scaling, documenting learnings that can be applied across accounts.

  • Travel may be required from time to time, including visits to customer office locations and company offices.

What You Have 

  • Proven track record of selling complex software solutions, with the ability to successfully execute on a consultative, solutions-oriented, value-based selling methodology. 

  • Excited about prospecting, and capable of independently leading a sales cycle from start to finish.

  • Ability to independently manage a pipeline, accurately forecast key sales performance metrics, and consistently maintain CRM hygiene.

  • Ability to lead a complex, multi-threaded sale with stakeholders ranging from executives across various functions to day-to-day product users – especially the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

  • Demonstrated passion for Harvey’s mission and strong understanding of AI and its potential applications in knowledge work. Interest in the legal profession and helping lawyers do their jobs better and more efficiently. 

  • Team player who can collaborate effectively across internal functions (product, legal, etc.) to achieve common goals.

  • Energized by contributing to the development of our team, sales processes, and culture, refining the value proposition of our solutions and creating sales resources to drive our success.

  • Experience working in or adjacent to the Legal industry a plus but not required.

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices [here].

As strategic partners to law firms and in-house teams, Legal Engineers thrive in ambiguity and help lawyers do higher-quality work faster and with more confidence using Harvey.

What You’ll Do

  • Work directly with lawyers at current and prospective customers to uncover workflow pain points, recommend solutions, and show how Harvey fits into real legal work.

  • Serve as the voice of the customer, translating feedback and legal workflow insights into concrete, lawyer-ready product direction.

  • Partner closely with product, engineering, sales, and marketing to shape Harvey’s roadmap and ensure the product evolves in ways lawyers trust and adopt.

  • Build and refine product demonstrations, workflows, and use cases that reflect how legal teams actually work, including how AI is changing that work.

  • Introduce new capabilities in a way that’s tailored, credible, and compelling for each customer, continuously raising the bar for how Harvey is deployed.

  • Provide competitive and market intelligence specific to the APAC legal tech landscape.

  • Further strengthen Harvey’s reputation in the APAC region as a credible, substantive, and forward-looking AI partner to the legal industry.

What You Have

You move confidently through uncertainty, you operate at speed, and ship solutions that work—iterating quickly with lawyers, sales teams, and product partners to help Harvey and its customers win. You bring deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform legal work, a bias towards action, and the creativity to solve problems nobody's cracked yet.

  • Based in Sydney and eligible to work in Australia.

  • Australian practising certificate (or equivalent common-law qualification).

  • At least 3 years of experience as a qualified lawyer at a top-tier law firm (e.g., Band 1 Chambers / AFR Top 10) and/or/in-house with strong exposure to complex legal workflows and client expectations.

  • Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and make confident, well-reasoned recommendations.

  • Ability to operate seamlessly across legal, product, and sales contexts—translating between stakeholders with clarity and precision.

  • Executive presence and relationship-building skills, with comfort engaging partners, senior associates, in-house counsel, and legal leadership.

  • Sales, customer-facing, or law firm business development experience is a plus, particularly where you’ve helped shape solutions rather than just present them.

Additional Information

  • Location: Sydney, NSW (Hybrid with flexibility)

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Australian work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role.

What We Offer

  • Structured hybrid working arrangement: 3 days in our Sydney office, 2 days working from home.

  • Health Coverage: Fully covered private hospital insurance, plus extras for dental, optical, physio, mental health, and more.

  • Family & Fertility Support: Support for fertility treatments, adoption, and surrogacy through Carrot.

  • Retirement & Security: Comprehensive coverage designed to support your long-term well-being.

  • Paid Leave: Paid annual leave, sick leave, and fully paid parental leave for all parents.

  • Wellness & Perks: Daily in-office lunch, wellness memberships through Wellhub, and monthly commuting support.

  • Professional Development: Annual support for courses, certifications, conferences, and books.

  • Remote Work Allowance: Monthly support for home office, internet, and phone expenses.

  • Harvey Holiday: After four years, enjoy a four-week paid sabbatical to rest, travel, or explore new experiences.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

The Technology Enablement Analyst joins Harvey's Technical Program Management team to drive how internal teams adopt, integrate, and realize value from enterprise technology platforms. The team's mission is to ensure Harvey's rapidly scaling workforce has frictionless access to the tools and systems that power their work, bridging the gap between BizTech and organizational productivity. This role is accountable for turning complex technical programs into clear, actionable enablement plans that different teams can execute against. They will own stakeholder alignment, rollout strategy, and ongoing iteration based on feedback and metrics. They will partner closely with product, engineering, customer success, and go-to-market teams to ensure that documentation, training, and communications effectively support behavior change at scale.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end-to-end enablement strategy for major internal technology initiatives, with an emphasis on internal AI tooling and related workflows

  • Monitor adoption, usage, and feedback, and use those insights to iterate on enablement plans, documentation, and training content

  • Plan and execute change management activities (e.g., communications, training, office hours) that drive adoption and sustained usage of new tools and processes

  • Build and maintain dashboards and reports that provide leadership with visibility into technology health, utilization, and ROI

  • Partner with all BizTech teams to evaluate new tools, drive integrations, and ensure smooth rollouts

  • Develop process documentation, runbooks, and training materials to support technology onboarding and change management

What You Have

  • At least 5 years of experience in technology‑enabled program delivery, technical training, or organization change management

  • Demonstrated track record leading change across multiple teams or functions (e.g., rolling out new tools, workflows, or processes)

  • Background in technology enablement, organization change management, or as a technical trainer, with comfort translating complex concepts for non‑technical audiences

  • Experience designing and maintaining program documentation or enablement materials as a single source of truth for diverse stakeholders

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

The Head of Technical Accounting and Reporting will own technical accounting, financial reporting, and internal controls in a dynamic, multi-product SaaS environment. This role is highly cross-functional, partnering closely with the Product, Sales, Legal, Partnerships, Revenue Accounting, Corporate Accounting and StratFin teams to ensure that new products, pricing structures, and commercial arrangements are accounted for accurately and in accordance with U.S. GAAP and, where applicable, IFRS. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving business, can bring structure and scalability to accounting operations, and can help lay the groundwork for future public-company readiness.

What You'll Do

Technical Accounting

  • Serve as the company's subject matter expert on complex accounting matters, researching and documenting positions in accordance with U.S. GAAP and, where applicable, IFRS.

  • Prepare clear, well-reasoned technical accounting memos on significant and non-routine transactions, including business combinations, equity and stock-based compensation, leases, and revenue arrangements.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams, including Product, Sales, Legal, and Partnerships, to assess the accounting implications of new partnerships, products, pricing structures, and other arrangements, and work with the Corporate and Revenue accounting teams to operationalize the accounting, and systematization of the accounting, for new agreements.

  • Monitor, assess, and implement new accounting standards and pronouncements, communicating the impact to senior management and other stakeholders.

  • Partner with external auditors and external technical accounting consultants to support the timely resolution of technical accounting questions and audit inquiries.

  • Evaluate the accounting impact of differences between U.S. GAAP and IFRS relevant to the company’s operations, including any dual-reporting, statutory, or foreign-subsidiary reporting requirements.

  • Own the company’s accounting policies and design and implementation of related controls including leases, stock-based compensation, business combinations, and revenue recognition (standalone selling price methodology, allocation of transaction price across performance obligations, and the timing and pattern of revenue recognition).

  • Assess material complex and non-standard contracts, including custom terms, usage-based pricing, and partner/reseller arrangements, and partner with the Revenue Accounting team to operationalize technical conclusions.

Financial Reporting and Controls

  • Own the preparation and review of internal and external financial statements, including footnote disclosures, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with U.S. GAAP and, where applicable, IFRS.

  • Design, implement, and maintain a scalable internal control environment, including documentation of key processes and controls, in preparation for future public-company readiness and SOX compliance.

  • Lead technical accounting and reporting workstreams in support of IPO readiness, including preparation of registration statement disclosures, coordination with underwriters and auditors, and remediation of legacy accounting positions.

  • Support the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes, driving improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and timeliness.

  • Develop and maintain accounting policies and procedures, ensuring consistent application across the organization.

  • Prepare reporting and analysis for senior leadership, the board, investors, and lenders as needed.

What You Have

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA required.

  • 15+ years of progressive accounting experience, including a combination of public accounting (Big 4 preferred) and industry experience.

  • Deep, current expertise in U.S. GAAP (including ASC 606 revenue recognition), with working knowledge of IFRS.

  • Prior experience in a SaaS, technology, or other high-growth environment strongly preferred.

  • Experience with technical accounting research and the preparation of technical memos on complex, non-routine transactions.

  • Working knowledge of internal controls and SOX, with experience supporting IPO readiness or public-company reporting a strong plus.

  • Strong understanding of technical accounting across areas such as business combinations, equity and stock-based compensation, leases, and revenue recognition.

Key Competencies

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex technical matters into clear, actionable guidance.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfortable partnering with both finance and non-finance stakeholders.

  • A hands-on, roll-up-your-sleeves mindset, with the ability to balance technical rigor against the practical needs of a fast-moving business.

  • Proven ability to build scalable processes and controls in an evolving environment.

  • High degree of ownership, integrity, and attention to detail.

Compensation

$224,000 - $336,000 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Role Overview

Harvey is looking for a Technical Revenue Accounting Lead to help us scale revenue recognition across a rapidly expanding portfolio of customer and partnership arrangements. Reporting to the Revenue Accounting Manager, this role will partner closely with Finance, Sales, Deal Desk, Legal, and Product and serve as the company’s subject-matter expert on ASC 606 and technical revenue accounting. In this highly collaborative, hands-on role, you'll review and help structure complex commercial contracts, author defensible accounting positions, and build the scalable processes, systems, and controls that will support Harvey through its next phases of growth. This is a high-impact opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving ambiguous problems, and is excited to help shape a best-in-class revenue accounting function.

What You'll Do

  • Provide technical accounting guidance on non-standard revenue transactions, including partnership agreements and complex subscription and usage-based deal structures

  • Evaluate the revenue accounting implications of new products, pricing models, and go-to-market motions, and advise cross-functional teams accordingly

  • Develop, document, and maintain revenue recognition policies, position papers, and accounting playbooks that scale with the business

  • Support month-end close processes and coordinate with external auditors

  • Help implement and optimize revenue systems and automation to improve accuracy, efficiency, and scalability

  • Design and maintain internal controls over revenue in support of audit and future SOX readiness

  • Assist with ad hoc financial reporting requests

What You Have

  • 3-5 years of experience in revenue accounting

  • CPA preferred

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

  • Experience in public accounting and at a high-growth technology company, with an emphasis in technical accounting.

  • Deep knowledge of ASC 606 and demonstrated experience applying guidance to non-standard contracts, including ASC 340-40 (costs to obtain a contract)

  • Demonstrated ability to write clear technical accounting memos. Can research guidance, state a position, and defend the conclusion

  • Proven ability to partner cross-functionally with Sales, Legal, Deal Desk, and Product in a fast-moving environment

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong analytical and problem-solving skills and comfort operating amid ambiguity

  • Experience with Netsuite and Netsuite ARM (or similar)

Compensation

$117,400 - $176,000 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Workplace Project Manager, you'll take our workplace playbooks and standards and turn them into delivered projects and programs on the ground - office moves and openings, and global special projects like health & safety programming, design standards, emergency response planning, WVPPs, sustainability, and new tooling rollouts. This is a hands-on delivery role: you own scope, schedule, and budget for each project or program and drive it from kickoff to close.

Where the program sets the standard, your projects and programs bring it to life - on time, on budget, and to spec.

What You'll Do

Global Special Projects

  • Project manage Workplace's global special projects: health & safety (H&S) programming, global design standards, global emergency response programming, Workplace Violence Prevention Plans (WVPPs), and sustainability programming across Harvey's office portfolio.

  • Partner with Security, HR, Legal, and regional Workplace leads to build and roll out emergency response plans and WVPPs that meet local regulatory requirements while staying consistent with Harvey's global standards.

  • Maintain and evolve global design standards (furniture, finishes, signage) so offices feel consistently "Harvey" as we scale into new markets.

  • Drive sustainability initiatives across offices - vendor and materials selection, energy and waste programs - and track progress against goals.

  • Own the global rollout of Workplace tooling and software - evaluating, piloting, and implementing platforms like desk booking, occupancy, and ticketing, and driving stakeholder training and adoption.

  • Own global and national vendor contracts (F&B, janitorial, plants, and similar categories) - procurement, negotiation, and the master vendor relationship - while regional workplace managers own the day-to-day relationship, performance, and feedback in their offices.


Global Playbook & Portfolio Management (Moves & Openings)

  • Build and maintain the FDOB checklist and playbook that regional workplace leads execute against for satellite moves, expansions, and new-office openings.

  • Own the portfolio-level calendar tracking when and where expansions and new offices are happening across the org, so Workplace can sequence and resource projects appropriately.

  • Step in to lead a move, opening, or buildout directly where a region doesn't yet have an established workplace manager, or where the existing regional team doesn't have the bandwidth - expect this to be a shrinking share of the role over time as regional coverage matures.

  • Coordinate with IT, Security, and AV to keep day-one readiness standards current in the playbook, so regional teams can deliver consistently without you running each project personally.

Program Management

  • Build and maintain project plans, schedules, and budgets across global programs and the FDOB playbook; track milestones, dependencies, and risks, and communicate status clearly to stakeholders and leadership.

  • Maintain the portfolio-level view across all in-flight and planned moves, openings, and buildouts, flagging sequencing and resourcing risks to leadership.

  • Manage vendor relationships tied to your global contracts and programs, holding them accountable to schedule and quality.

  • Report to the Global Workplace Operations Manager to ensure every program and playbook meets Harvey's workplace standards and sets regional teams up for smooth steady-state operations.

What You Have

  • 5+ years in workplace operations, program management, or project management, with experience leading cross-functional programs such as health & safety, emergency preparedness, sustainability, or systems/tooling rollouts.

  • Strong program design and playbook-building instincts - you'd rather build a system and standard that others execute against well than run every project yourself.

  • Experience managing vendor and procurement relationships at a national or global scale.

  • Strong command of project management fundamentals - scope, schedule, budget, risk, and stakeholder communication.

  • Experience partnering with (not necessarily owning) construction, real estate, or facilities teams on office moves or buildouts.

  • Excellent organizational and communication skills; you keep complex, fast-moving programs on track and everyone informed.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a hands-on, get-it-done approach.

  • Based in New York and able to work on-site at our NYC office, with willingness to travel to other sites as projects require.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building or administering H&S programs, emergency response plans, or WVPPs.

  • Experience with sustainability program design or reporting.

  • Familiarity with project / workplace tools - e.g., Asana, Smartsheet, Envoy, OfficeSpace.

  • Experience building playbooks or programs that scale across a distributed, multi-region team.

Compensation

$120,900 - $181,300 USD

 - Partner with Security, HR, Legal, and regional Workplace leads to build and roll out emergency response plans and WVPPs that meet local regulatory requirements while staying consistent with Harvey's global standards.

 - Maintain and evolve global design standards (furniture, finishes, signage) so offices feel consistently "Harvey" as we scale into new markets.

 - Drive sustainability initiatives across offices - vendor and materials selection, energy and waste programs - and track progress against goals.

 - Own the global rollout of Workplace tooling and software - evaluating, piloting, and implementing platforms like desk booking, occupancy, and ticketing, and driving stakeholder training and adoption.

 - Own global and national vendor contracts (F&B, janitorial, plants, and similar categories) - procurement, negotiation, and the master vendor relationship - while regional workplace managers own the day-to-day relationship, performance, and feedback in their offices.

 - Build and maintain the FDOB checklist and playbook that regional workplace leads execute against for satellite moves, expansions, and new-office openings.

 - Own the portfolio-level calendar tracking when and where expansions and new offices are happening across the org, so Workplace can sequence and resource projects appropriately.

Program Management



 - Build and maintain project plans, schedules, and budgets across global programs and the FDOB playbook; track milestones, dependencies, and risks, and communicate status clearly to stakeholders and leadership.

 - Maintain the portfolio-level view across all in-flight and planned moves, openings, and buildouts, flagging sequencing and resourcing risks to leadership.

 - Manage vendor relationships tied to your global contracts and programs, holding them accountable to schedule and quality.

 - Report to the Global Workplace Operations Manager to ensure every program and playbook meets Harvey's workplace standards and sets regional teams up for smooth steady-state operations.







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Experience managing vendor and procurement relationships at a national or global scale.

 - Strong command of project management fundamentals - scope, schedule, budget, risk, and stakeholder communication.

 - Excellent organizational and communication skills; you keep complex, fast-moving programs on track and everyone informed.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with sustainability program design or reporting.

 - Experience building playbooks or programs that scale across a distributed, multi-region team.

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is seeking an Integrations Engineer, Enterprise Systems to build and maintain the integrations that connect our core business systems. You will design, implement, test, and monitor workflows across systems such as Salesforce, CPQ, NetSuite, Workday, Marketo, Snowflake, and iPaaS platforms, with a focus on data quality, operational reliability, and business impact. You will partner closely with Finance Systems, GTM Systems, People Ops, RevOps, and IT stakeholders to translate business requirements into durable technical solutions. You should be comfortable working hands-on with APIs, scripts, data transformations, error handling, and integration monitoring while communicating clearly with both technical and non-technical partners. This is the third Integrations Engineer hire, and you will work closely with Sriharsha Gurram, the Lead Integrations Engineer, to develop the foundations and architecture of the integrations function.

This is a builder role for someone who enjoys making business-critical systems more reliable, scalable, and understandable. The ideal candidate has enough technical depth to debug integration failures and write scripts, enough systems judgment to avoid creating long-term tech debt, and enough stakeholder empathy to help teams make tradeoffs when speed, accuracy, and scalability compete.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain integrations between core enterprise systems including Salesforce, CPQ, NetSuite, Workday, Marketo, Snowflake, and related business applications.

  • Develop data pipelines, workflow automations, and reverse ETL-style syncs that help GTM, Finance, People Ops, and other teams operate from trusted data.

  • Translate business requirements into integration designs, data mappings, and implementation plans that are scalable, observable, and maintainable.

  • Troubleshoot data sync issues, schema mismatches, API failures, and workflow exceptions across multiple systems.

  • Implement strong error handling, logging, alerting, validation, rollback, and documentation practices for business-critical workflows.

  • Partner with Finance Systems and GTM Systems stakeholders on Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, order management, billing, and reporting workflows.

  • Partner with People Ops and IT stakeholders on employee lifecycle and identity-adjacent workflows where enterprise systems need accurate, automated data movement.

  • Document integration designs, dependencies, runbooks, and operational procedures so the team can scale beyond heroics and single-owner knowledge.

  • Support integration platform standards for API usage, data modeling, monitoring, and production readiness under the guidance of the Lead Integration Engineer or hiring manager.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain integrations between core enterprise systems including Salesforce, CPQ, NetSuite, Workday, Marketo, Snowflake, and related business applications.

  • Develop data pipelines, workflow automations, and reverse ETL-style syncs that help GTM, Finance, People Ops, and other teams operate from trusted data.

  • Translate business requirements into integration designs, data mappings, and implementation plans that are scalable, observable, and maintainable.

  • Troubleshoot data sync issues, schema mismatches, API failures, and workflow exceptions across multiple systems.

  • Implement strong error handling, logging, alerting, validation, rollback, and documentation practices for business-critical workflows.

  • Partner with Finance Systems and GTM Systems stakeholders on Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, order management, billing, and reporting workflows.

  • Partner with People Ops and IT stakeholders on employee lifecycle and identity-adjacent workflows where enterprise systems need accurate, automated data movement.

  • Document integration designs, dependencies, runbooks, and operational procedures so the team can scale beyond heroics and single-owner knowledge.

  • Support integration platform standards for API usage, data modeling, monitoring, and production readiness under the guidance of the Lead Integration Engineer or hiring manager.

 

What You Have

  • You have 3–5+ years of experience in integration engineering, software engineering, business systems engineering, or a related backend systems role.

  • You have hands-on experience working within an iPaaS platform (e.g. Workato) to build or maintain integrations across enterprise SaaS systems, ideally including Salesforce, NetSuite, Workday, Ashby, Marketo, Snowflake, or comparable platforms.

  • You understand modern API patterns and authentication concepts, including REST, SOAP, GraphQL, OAuth, SAML, SCIM, and related integration standards.

  • You can write scripts in Python, JavaScript, or a similar language to handle transformations, validation, orchestration, or automation logic.

  • You have strong troubleshooting instincts and can work systematically through logs, data mismatches, failed syncs, and edge cases.

  • You know how to communicate tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders and can push back when a requested solution would create fragility, governance issues, or unnecessary tech debt.

  • You are comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where requirements may be ambiguous, priorities may shift, and systems may still be maturing.

  • You have a bias toward pragmatic execution, but you also care about building repeatable patterns, documentation, and operational safeguards.

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience with reverse ETL concepts and data warehousing workflows is a plus.

  • Familiarity with Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, CPQ, order management, billing, revenue recognition, or ERP workflows is a plus.

  • Experience in high-growth B2B SaaS, legal tech, enterprise AI, or other environments with complex cross-functional systems is a plus.

  • Exposure to identity lifecycle, provisioning, or access-related integrations is useful but not required.

Compensation

$133,500 - $200,300 USD

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are hiring a hands-on leader to own how Harvey designs its GTM incentive strategy for its go-to-market organization. As Head of GTM Incentive Strategy, you will design the incentive architecture that turns our revenue strategy into the plans, quotas, and payouts that motivate and reward our sellers. This is a design-first, high-ownership role: you will set the compensation philosophy, build the plans, and put the modeling and governance in place to keep them fair, motivating, and defensible as we scale.

What You'll Do

  • Own the end to end design of GTM incentive compensation across both pre- and post-sales organizations, including quota carrying AEs, sales leadership, solutions and overlay teams, customer success, etc.

  • Build the models that forecast plan cost, incentive ROI, and attainment distribution; run scenario analysis to stress-test designs before they ship and diagnose plans already in market

  • Partner with Compensation Business Partner to align OTE, pay mix, and leverage to market benchmarks and internal equity, and to keep plan spend inside budget

  • Set and communicate the compensation philosophy: produce executive-ready narratives on plan performance and risk, and educate GTM leaders and sellers so plans drive the behavior they are designed to reward

  • Architect plan mechanics that scale with hypergrowth, including quota structures, accelerators, multipliers, and SPIFFs

  • Translate GTM strategy changes - new segments, product and pricing launches, territory and coverage-model shifts - into comp plan updates delivered with speed and accuracy

  • Partner with compensation admin team on the ICM platform, quota-to-payout reconciliation, payout automation, and real-time earnings visibility for sellers and managers

  • Establish the governance layer - plan documentation, cross-functional approval workflows, version control, and audit-ready practices - and lead dispute resolution with clear SLAs and consistent outcomes

  • Partner with Finance on how goals translate to outcomes and the subsequent incentive strategy

What You Have

  • 10+ years in sales/incentive compensation design, revenue operations, or a closely related field, with demonstrated experience owning plan design at scale in a B2B SaaS environment

  • Deep, hands-on expertise designing incentive structures sales organizations - accelerators, SPIFFs, overlays, and co-sell frameworks

  • Strong analytical and modeling skills, with the ability to structure ambiguous questions, work with incomplete data, and quantify the cost and ROI of design decisions

  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Finance, People, and Legal through clear communication, strong judgment, and data-backed recommendations

  • Comfort operating autonomously as a leader and function owner - setting direction and building the function directly, with or without a team beneath you

  • Bonus: experience in high-growth or hypergrowth organizations, with consumption- or usage-based pricing dynamics, or in AI / legal technology

Compensation

$212,000 - $300,000 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

The Head of Recruiting Coordination joins Harvey's Talent team to lead and scale the recruiting coordination function across the company's global offices. The team's mission is to deliver an exceptional candidate experience while driving operational efficiency throughout the interview lifecycle.

This role owns the strategy and execution for recruiting coordination programs, automation initiatives, and process improvement that enable Harvey to hire world-class talent at the pace a hypergrowth AI company demands. They partner directly with recruiting leadership, People Operations, and systems teams to architect scalable workflows that maintain a high-quality bar as the organization grows. It is a rare opportunity to build and lead a coordination function at a company redefining an industry through AI.

What You'll Do

  • Lead, mentor, and manage a team of recruiting coordinators across multiple offices, setting standards for candidate experience, interview logistics, and operational excellence.

  • Own internal recruiting programs including interviewer enablement, onboarding for new interviewers, and coordination training.

  • Own Tier 1 operational backlog, including things like creating and closing job requisitions, ATS data upkeep, interview plan maintenance, etc.

  • Design and implement process improvements within tier one operations that reduce friction for recruiters, hiring managers, and candidates

  • Partner with Recruiting Operations on ATS architecture, workflow optimization, and data integrity to support hiring at scale.

  • Develop and maintain metrics and dashboards that track coordination team performance, candidate experience, and process efficiency.

  • Serve as an escalation point for scheduling and coordination issues, ensuring a consistently high-quality candidate and interviewer experience

What You Have

  • 5–8+ years of experience in recruiting operations or coordination, with progressive team management responsibility.

  • Demonstrated success building and managing a coordination team in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

  • Deep expertise in ATS platforms (e.g., Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever) and workflow automation tools.

  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to use data to drive process improvements and inform stakeholder decisions.

  • Excellent cross-functional communication skills and the ability to influence without authority across recruiting, People Operations, and hiring manager stakeholders.

Compensation

$180,000- $220,000 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Role Overview

The Workplace Manager joins Harvey's global Workplace Operations team to own and elevate the day-to-day experience of Harvey's Sydney office. The team's mission is to deliver a consistently high-quality, operationally seamless environment across every Harvey location worldwide. This role is responsible for shaping the physical environment, vendor relationships, and office culture that enable Harvey's growing APAC presence to thrive. The Workplace Manager partners closely with People Operations, IT, and local leadership to ensure the Sydney office runs at the standard employees experience in Harvey's more established locations. It is a unique opportunity to build the playbook for a scaling satellite office at one of the fastest-growing companies in legal AI.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end workplace operations for Harvey's Sydney office, including facilities management, vendor coordination, and office logistics

  • Develop and implement local workplace programs, events, and initiatives that foster a productive, welcoming employee experience

  • Manage relationships with building management, service vendors, and contractors, ensuring quality, cost-effectiveness, and compliance with local regulations

  • Partner cross-functionally with People Operations, IT, Finance, and local leadership to align workplace strategy with broader business needs

  • Contribute to global workplace standards and playbooks, adapting them for the APAC region while maintaining consistency across Harvey's offices

What You Have

  • 3+ years of experience in workplace operations, office management, or facilities coordination, ideally in a high-growth or technology environment

  • Demonstrated ability to manage vendor relationships, budgets, and office build-outs or transitions

  • Strong organizational skills with a bias for action and meticulous attention to detail

  • Experience operating autonomously in a smaller or satellite office setting while aligning to global standards

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to partner across time zones and functions

Additional Information

  • Location: Sydney, NSW (Hybrid with flexibility)

  • Work eligibility: Must have valid Australian work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

What We Offer

  • Structured hybrid working arrangement: 3 days in our Sydney office, 2 days working from home

  • Health Coverage: Fully covered private hospital insurance, plus extras for dental, optical, physio, mental health, and more.

  • Family & Fertility Support: Support for fertility treatments, adoption, and surrogacy through Carrot.

  • Retirement & Security: Comprehensive coverage designed to support your long-term well-being.

  • Paid Leave: Paid annual leave, sick leave, and fully paid parental leave for all parents.

  • Wellness & Perks: Daily in-office lunch, wellness memberships through Wellhub, and monthly commuting support.

  • Professional Development: Annual support for courses, certifications, conferences, and books.

  • Remote Work Allowance: Monthly support for home office, internet, and phone expenses.

  • Harvey Holiday: After four years, enjoy a four-week paid sabbatical to rest, travel, or explore new experiences.
