ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey's Employee Experience team was recently established, and you’d be one of its first hires reporting to the Employee Experience Lead. Previously, individual offices ran their own events independently, and swag was made ad hoc. As Harvey has grown to more than a dozen global offices, it’s building a centralized team to design and run employee experience programs consistently across every location.



You’d join at an early stage of that transition. Harvey just ran its first company-wide event spanning 13 offices simultaneously: its 4th Anniversary Celebration. Up next, the team is designing family-oriented events, wellness events, 13+ holiday parties, and even a round-the-world leadership tour. You'll support that planning directly. Much of the work is establishing processes and programs that don't yet exist in their final form, rather than running an established playbook.



You’ll combine hands-on event logistics, company-wide engagement and recognition programs, and vendor coordination, all while tailoring programming across offices of different sizes, cultures, and preferences (for example, adjusting activities based on what a given office's employees actually enjoy).







WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Global signature events, end to end — company anniversaries, holiday parties, and other company-wide moments. You'll be the connective tissue between a central creative vision and 13+ very different offices, working with local vendors and event planners to make each one feel tailored, not templated.

 - On-the-ground execution in New York — you're the person actually in the room: managing vendors, confirming the mic works before leadership speaks, solving the problem nobody planned for.

 - Recognition and milestones — birthdays, work anniversaries, milestone gifting, and the full operational engine of Harvey Honors (nominations, logistics, fulfillment). You'll own the systems that make sure nothing slips through the cracks, so every moment that matters lands on time and feels personal.

 - Swag — from new-hire kits to on-brand gear, plus our new self-serve swag store. You’ll help stand it up and run it as the place employees claim their own gear, keeping the whole program feeling intentional and on-brand.

 - Harvey Hangouts — our recurring small-group connection program, coordinating facilitators, managing the budget, tracking participation, and running U.S. events from venue booking through wrap-up.

 - The company-wide events calendar and theming — you set the themes, timing, and guidelines that every office uses, while local Workplace teams handle small, office-specific execution.

 - The unglamorous operational backbone that makes all of this work — RSVPs, dietary and accessibility needs, contracts, invoices, shipping, budget tracking, and flagging variances before they become a problem.

 - Feedback loops — surveys, pulse checks, and focus groups that tell us whether any of this is actually landing, and shape what we do next.

You'll have real creative latitude here. There's no fixed formula for what a "great Harvey experience" looks like yet — you'll help define it, propose ideas, and even A/B test approaches, always in service of making things feel high-touch and genuinely personal rather than corporate.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Customer Education sits within Product and owns the front door through which every Harvey customer comes to understand the product. The team already runs a strong certification program and a content library our customers trust, and partners constantly with Product, Product Operations, Sales, Legal Engineering and Customer Success to keep it that way.

We're hiring a Head of Customer Learning to take ownership of an evolving Customer Education team and elevate the function into a strategic, revenue-relevant part of the business. The foundation is strong: an Academy, certification program and content library our customers already trust. This role is about scaling that foundation, setting a multi-quarter roadmap, and owning exec-level updates for Customer Education.

You'll partner closely with Product, Customer Experience, Product Operations, and GTM leadership to align the roadmap to the business, build out a digital-first strategy for onboarding and adoption, and develop the longer-term vision for how Harvey teaches an entire industry to work with AI - positioning Harvey as the definitive authority on Legal AI education along the way.

What You'll Do

  • Roadmap and executive alignment - partner with Product, Product Operations, and GTM leadership to define and own the Customer Education roadmap, and represent the function in executive-level updates and decisions.

  • Team leadership and scale - lead and grow the existing Customer Education team, including its current lead, as Harvey's customer base and product surface area expand - building the org structure, hiring plan, and contractor/agency or in-house train-the-trainer model to match.

  • Content strategy and portfolio health - own the lifecycle, governance, discoverability, and quality bar of Harvey's education content as the portfolio scales, so Sales, CS, and Support can always find and trust the right resource.

  • Certification and learning programs - own and evolve Harvey's existing certification program and Academy, expanding curriculum depth and coverage as new products and workflows launch.

  • Digital adoption strategy - design and run the multi-channel, digital-first strategy that drives onboarding and adoption - in-product guidance, digital nurture and engagement sequences, webinars, video, and community - treating activation and expansion as a funnel to measure and improve.

  • Legal AI thought leadership - develop the vision and content strategy for how Harvey teaches the legal industry to work with AI, and position Harvey as the definitive authority on Legal AI education through external-facing content, programs, and points of view.

  • Metrics and systems - own north-star metrics for the function - time-to-value, activation/adoption depth, certification and adoption velocity, ticket deflection, and education's contribution to NRR - and partner with Product and Data to instrument what's working.

What You Have

  • 10+ years of experience in customer education, learning/academy functions, content strategy, or digital-led customer engagement, including real experience scaling a function beyond its initial build into a strategic, revenue-relevant program.

  • Comfortable operating at both altitudes: setting a multi-quarter roadmap and owning exec-level updates, while staying close enough to the work to raise the bar on content, certification, and digital programs.

  • Experience partnering with Product, Product Operations, and GTM/Sales leadership to align a customer-facing function to business priorities and turn that into a roadmap.

  • A digital-first instinct for adoption and onboarding - thinks in funnels, touchpoints, and journeys across in-product guidance, digital communications, and content.

  • Strong content and program operations judgment: portfolio governance, lifecycle management, and quality standards.

  • A point of view on building thought leadership and market authority through education and content - ideally developed in a specialized, regulated, or traditionally low-software-adoption industry.

  • Data-driven - comfortable owning dashboards and making the case that education and adoption are leading indicators of revenue.

  • Proven people leadership: has hired, developed, and led teams (including other leads or managers) and has managed external contractor or agency relationships.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with real experience presenting to and influencing senior executives.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in legal, professional services, financial services, or another industry where customers are newer to AI-native software.

  • Familiarity with LMS platforms, authoring tools, and in-product engagement tools.

  • Experience building executive point-of-view content or category-defining thought leadership programs.

  • Experience using AI tools to scale content production or personalize learning paths.

Compensation

$184,000 - $276,000 USD

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.


Role Overview

The Global Benefits and Leaves Analyst joins Harvey's Total Rewards team to support administering and improving employee benefits and leave programs across a rapidly scaling, global workforce. The team's mission is to deliver competitive, compliant, and employee-centric programs in every region where Harvey operates. This role manages day-to-day Tier 1 benefits support globally while partnering on benefits programs and vendor operations across EMEA and APAC, ensuring employees receive timely, accurate guidance and that programs run smoothly as Harvey expands into new markets. You’ll work closely with People Operations, Payroll, and external brokers, building operational rigor into a function that directly touches every employee. It is a chance to scale benefit operations at a category-defining AI company during a period of exceptional international growth.


What You'll Do

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for Tier 1 global benefits inquiries across all regions (including the US) with a responsive, service-oriented approach—resolving standard requests directly while escalating complex cases to the Benefits Program Managers.

  • Assist in administration and support of benefits programs and vendor relationships across EMEA and APAC, ensuring compliance with local regulations and alignment with Harvey's total rewards philosophy.

  • Coordinate leave-of-absence processes end-to-end — including statutory and company-provided leaves — across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Partner with Payroll and external brokers to ensure accurate benefits enrollment, changes, and offboarding workflows.

  • Analyze benefits utilization data and employee queries to identify trends and propose process improvements.

  • Partner with Benefit Program Managers on open enrollment execution, new-country benefit launches, and drafting employee communications.

  • Track, process, and reconcile benefits-related invoices from vendors and brokers.

  • Develop, maintain and update internal benefits documentation, employee FAQs, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) as programs scale.

  • Coordinate vendor onboarding, administrative PO creation, and contract workflows with guidance from Finance and Legal


What You Have

  • 2–4 years of experience in benefits administration, leave management, or a related HR operations role, ideally within a global or multi-country environment

  • Working knowledge of EMEA and/or APAC benefits structures, statutory requirements, and leave entitlements

  • Excellent communication and service orientation, with a track record of delivering responsive, empathetic employee support

  • Experience working with HRIS platforms (e.g., Workday), HR ticketing or case management systems (e.g., ServiceNow, Zendesk, Jira, or Workday Help), and benefits administration tools

  • Experience or exposure to benefits vendor/broker management

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret benefits data and produce actionable insights

  • Ability to manage day-to-day workflows independently while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate complex issues

  • Proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (vlookups, pivot tables) for basic data analysis and invoice reconciliation

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We're hiring a Senior People Operations Generalist to join our global People Operations team. You'll support our entire global population — onboarding, compliance, day-to-day HR questions — in true partnership with the rest of the team, with work divided by focus area rather than by region. You'll also take on our global compliance programs almost like a program manager: building them, maintaining them, and continuously improving how they run as we scale into new countries.

Based in Ireland or the UK, your experience and time zone will naturally make you the go-to person for EMEA and JAPAC coverage — making calls in real time while the rest of the team is offline. You'll report to our Senior Manager, People Operations and join a broader team of People Operations Generalists and Coordinators. This is a senior generalist role for someone who wants real ownership of a global function, with the backing of a larger team behind them.


What You'll Do

  • Support the end-to-end employee lifecycle for our global population: onboarding, changes, leaves, exits, and everything in between, as part of a global team with work divided by function and program rather than region alone

  • Own our global compliance programs like a program manager: build new processes, maintain and improve existing ones (right-to-work, statutory leave, GDPR/data protection, and more), and drive ongoing efficiency as we add countries

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for employees, managers, and external partners (brokers, EOR providers, government agencies) during EMEA/JAPAC hours, given your time zone and regional expertise

  • Partner with global payroll and EOR platforms (Deel, Remote, or similar) to manage country-specific new hire and offboarding requirements worldwide

  • Build and maintain SOPs so global processes are documented and don't depend on tribal knowledge

  • Represent the broader People Ops team on EMEA/JAPAC matters, using good judgment about what needs to wait for US hours and what doesn't

  • Partner cross-functionally with People Systems, Legal, IT, Payroll, and Workplace teams based in the US


What You Have

  • 4–6 years of HR/People Ops experience, ideally including time in a mature, multi-country organization

  • Experience running compliance like a program: building, maintaining, and improving processes over time, not just administering them

  • Strong, hands-on knowledge of employment law and compliance in at least one region outside the US — EMEA and/or JAPAC experience preferred, given the time zone value it brings

  • Working knowledge of GDPR and HR data protection requirements

  • Experience with HRIS/payroll platforms such as Workday, Deel, or Remote

  • A track record of working independently across a global, distributed team, with good instincts about when to escalate and when to just handle it

  • A strategic mindset with a strong inclination for program and project management

  • Excellent written communication, given the async nature of working across time zones

  • Comfort being the go-to point of contact for a region during your hours, and the confidence to represent the function externally

jobs.descriptionHtml:

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey is seeking highly strategic, proactive, and polished Executive Assistants to support senior leaders across the organization. This role goes beyond traditional administrative support. It requires a partner who can help maximize executive leverage, operate as a force multiplier, and bring structure to a fast-moving, high-stakes environment.

The ideal candidate has experience supporting senior, externally-facing executives and is comfortable navigating complex stakeholder landscapes across internal teams, customers, and partners. This person exercises strong judgment, is highly discerning about priorities, and plays an active role in ensuring the executive’s time is deployed against the highest-impact opportunities. They bring a track record of owning executive time, acting as an opinionated partner, and helping drive meaningful business outcomes.

What You'll Do

  • Drive executive leverage by owning and optimizing complex calendars, ensuring time is allocated to the highest-priority internal and external engagements

  • Act as a strategic gatekeeper for the executive’s time, triaging inbound requests, prioritizing effectively, and making clear, confident recommendations on where attention is needed

  • Operate and scale the executive request flow, bringing structure and clarity across a wide set of stakeholders and ensuring efficient intake, prioritization, and follow-through

  • Serve as a central point of coordination across internal teams and external stakeholders, ensuring communication is seamless, proactive, and high quality while maintaining strong relationships

  • Own meeting preparation end to end, including agenda setting, materials development, and driving follow-ups to ensure strong execution and momentum

  • Manage complex inboxes and communications, helping synthesize information, draft responses, and ensure the executive is consistently well-prepared and ahead by surfacing key decisions and recommending actions

  • Plan and execute high-impact travel and logistics with a focus on efficiency, foresight, and minimizing friction

  • Support strategic projects and initiatives, bringing organization, follow-through, and a bias for action

  • Contribute to presentations and materials, ensuring executive communications are clear, polished, and aligned to priorities

  • Act as a steady, calm, and positive presence across a broad set of relationships, helping maintain alignment and trust

  • Handle highly sensitive and confidential information with discretion and sound judgment

What You Have

  • 3+ years of experience supporting senior executives, ideally in a high-growth, externally-facing environment, with a strong preference for experience supporting C-level or equivalent leaders

  • Proven ability to manage complex stakeholder ecosystems, including senior external partners and cross-functional internal teams

  • Strong judgment and prioritization skills, with the ability to triage competing demands and make clear, confident decisions on behalf of the executive

  • Experience managing high-volume, complex inboxes and communications, with a focus on creating leverage and clarity while proactively driving decision-making

  • Track record of building and operating scalable systems for managing requests, workflows, and executive engagement

  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to draft executive-level messaging and engage credibly with senior stakeholders

  • High degree of professionalism and executive presence, with the ability to influence and build trust across all levels of an organization

  • Calm, steady, and solutions-oriented under pressure, with the ability to bring structure to ambiguous situations

  • Highly proactive and resourceful, with a strong ownership mindset and bias for action

  • Discreet and trustworthy when handling sensitive information

Compensation

$113,000 - $169,600 USD

jobs.title: Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

As a Product Designer on the Design Systems team at Harvey, you will support in defining the foundations that make our product coherent, scalable, and trustworthy as it grows in complexity. The design system is not just a library of components. It is the shared language between design, engineering, and AI that ensures consistency, quality, and confidence across every interaction.

This is an ideal role for someone who loves precision, consistency, and execution, operating as a hands-on builder and trusted partner to the Design Systems team. Working closely with product designers and frontend engineers, you will craft, maintain, and scale the components, patterns, documentation, and system assets that power Harvey's product, improving the quality, consistency, and speed with which teams build.

We're looking for someone who thrives in fast-moving environments, has exceptional attention to detail, and takes pride in producing thoughtful, polished work. As the Design Systems team continues to grow, you'll help shape not only the system itself, but also the processes, workflows, and ways of working that enable the team to scale successfully.

 

Why Design Systems matter at Harvey

Harvey is an AI-native product. As the system reasons, responds, and adapts in real time, the interface must remain consistent and legible. A strong design system ensures that complexity does not leak into the experience. It enables teams to move faster, reduces cognitive load for users, and builds trust in moments where clarity matters most.

 

What You'll Do

  • Build, maintain, and evolve production-ready design system components, patterns, documentation, and reusable assets across Figma and emerging AI-native design workflows.

  • Partner with the Senior Design Systems Designer to scale Harvey's visual language and support the rollout of new system foundations across the product.

  • Collaborate with product designers and frontend engineers to ensure system components are intuitive to use, accurately implemented, and consistently adopted.

  • Own and create polished production assets, libraries, prototypes, and documentation that enable teams to build quickly and with confidence.

  • Support AI-assisted design workflows by preparing components, documentation, and system assets that are optimized for both designers and AI tools.

  • Maintain the quality and health of the design system through QA, organization, continuous refinement, and operational improvements.

  • Advocate for exceptional craftsmanship, consistency, and usability across every product surface.

 

What You Have

  • 3–5 years of experience as a Product Designer, Production Designer, UI Designer, or Design Systems Designer working on digital products.

  • Exceptional visual craft with a meticulous eye for detail, layout, spacing, consistency, and production quality.

  • Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams while maintaining a high quality bar.

  • Experience building and maintaining component libraries and design systems in Figma, including auto layout, variables, components, and variants.

  • Curiosity and experience in AI-assisted design tools and evolving implementation workflows, you don't need to be an engineer, but you're excited about where the discipline is heading.

  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a desire to learn through close partnership with design and engineering.

  • Comfort working in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment and enthusiasm for helping shape an evolving Design Systems practice.

 

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

As a Product Designer on the Design Systems team at Harvey, you will support in defining the foundations that make our product coherent, scalable, and trustworthy as it grows in complexity. The design system is not just a library of components. It is the shared language between design, engineering, and AI that ensures consistency, quality, and confidence across every interaction.

This is an ideal role for someone who loves precision, consistency, and execution, operating as a hands-on builder and trusted partner to the Design Systems team. Working closely with product designers and frontend engineers, you will craft, maintain, and scale the components, patterns, documentation, and system assets that power Harvey's product, improving the quality, consistency, and speed with which teams build.

We're looking for someone who thrives in fast-moving environments, has exceptional attention to detail, and takes pride in producing thoughtful, polished work. As the Design Systems team continues to grow, you'll help shape not only the system itself, but also the processes, workflows, and ways of working that enable the team to scale successfully.

Why Design Systems matter at Harvey

Harvey is an AI-native product. As the system reasons, responds, and adapts in real time, the interface must remain consistent and legible. A strong design system ensures that complexity does not leak into the experience. It enables teams to move faster, reduces cognitive load for users, and builds trust in moments where clarity matters most.

What You'll Do

  • Build, maintain, and evolve production-ready design system components, patterns, documentation, and reusable assets across Figma and emerging AI-native design workflows.

  • Partner with the Senior Design Systems Designer to scale Harvey's visual language and support the rollout of new system foundations across the product.

  • Collaborate with product designers and frontend engineers to ensure system components are intuitive to use, accurately implemented, and consistently adopted.

  • Own and create polished production assets, libraries, prototypes, and documentation that enable teams to build quickly and with confidence.

  • Support AI-assisted design workflows by preparing components, documentation, and system assets that are optimized for both designers and AI tools.

  • Maintain the quality and health of the design system through QA, organization, continuous refinement, and operational improvements.

  • Advocate for exceptional craftsmanship, consistency, and usability across every product surface.

  • 3–5 years of experience as a Product Designer, Production Designer, UI Designer, or Design Systems Designer working on digital products.

  • Exceptional visual craft with a meticulous eye for detail, layout, spacing, consistency, and production quality.

  • Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple workstreams while maintaining a high quality bar.

  • Experience building and maintaining component libraries and design systems in Figma, including auto layout, variables, components, and variants.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are hiring a Partner Manager to help operationalize and scale Harvey’s legal partnerships. This role will own the day-to-day management and execution of legal partnerships, ensuring each one translates into a clear, repeatable go-to-market motion.

You will work closely with Harvey’s legal partners and internal teams across Sales, Enablement, and Customer Success to develop joint GTM plans, enable partner teams, coordinate customer opportunities, establish governance and operating cadences, and track performance against shared goals.

The ideal candidate is a strong, detail-oriented operator who can bring structure to complex partnerships, drive cross-functional execution, and ensure partners are engaged and delivering measurable commercial value. They are equally comfortable managing strategic partner relationships and owning the operational work required to make those partnerships successful.

What You'll Do

  • Manage the day-to-day execution of select partnerships, including partner onboarding, enablement, joint planning, and ongoing program management.

  • Build strong working relationships with partner stakeholders and serve as a consistent point of contact across active initiatives.

  • Coordinate across cross-functional teams like Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Product to ensure partner commitments are executed effectively.

  • Develop clear project plans, operating cadences, partner materials, and internal processes that make partnership programs scalable and repeatable.

  • Track partner activity, pipeline, engagement, and program performance, and provide clear updates to internal stakeholders.

  • Drive partner sourced pipeline to achieve pipeline generation targets and company goals.

  • Gather feedback from partners, customers, and internal teams to improve existing programs and inform future partnership strategy.

  • Support partner-facing meetings, business reviews, training sessions, and executive updates

What You Have

  • 5-7 years of professional experience in partnerships, consulting, business operations, strategy, sales, customer success, or a related field.

  • High attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership.

  • Strong program management skills, including the ability to manage multiple workstreams, establish clear owners and timelines, and drive follow-through from planning through execution.

  • Proven ability to build strong relationships with external stakeholders.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information and communicate clear recommendations.

  • Strong business judgment and the ability to operate effectively in ambiguous situations.

  • Ability to influence and maintain momentum across teams with competing priorities.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth, and highly collaborative environment.

Compensation

$160,000 - $230,000 USD

This role drives the operational backbone behind cross-functional web initiatives — managing roadmaps, vendors, and capacity across engineering, design, creative, and marketing stakeholders to ship high-quality digital experiences on time and at scale.   • Own end-to-end program management for Harvey's digital experience portfolio — from requirements gathering and roadmap planning through delivery and retrospective.

  • Manage vendor relationships, capacity planning, and resource allocation to maximize the team's throughput without sacrificing craft.

  • Establish and maintain accountability mechanisms — status reporting, dependency tracking, and escalation paths — that keep stakeholders aligned in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

The Staff Web Developer joins Harvey's Web team as the senior technical leader for the architecture, data foundations, and systems integration behind harvey.ai and every web-facing surface. The team's mission is to make Harvey's web presence evolve at the velocity of the product itself — reliable, observable, and fast enough that Marketing and GTM can ship without waiting on engineering.

This role owns the technical strategy for that platform: the Next.js and Sanity architecture, the integration layer connecting the website to Harvey's marketing, analytics, and GTM systems, and the automation and testing practices the team currently lacks. You will be the most senior engineer on a small, front-end-leaning team, setting standards and mentoring as much as building.

You partner directly with Harvey's product engineering, security, and infrastructure organizations to make sure the web platform meets the same bar as the rest of the company. It is a rare opportunity to build foundational systems from scratch at one of the fastest-growing AI companies, with unusually direct line of sight from your work to the company's growth.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the architecture of Harvey's web platform end to end — the Next.js/Vercel application, the Sanity content layer, and the services and APIs behind them — with a focus on reliability, performance, and scalability.

  • Design and build the data foundations and integration patterns that connect the website to Harvey's marketing, analytics, CRM, and GTM systems, supporting both real-time and batch workloads.

  • Establish automation, CI/CD, preview/deploy tooling, and robust automated testing where little exists today, reducing operational toil and increasing team velocity.

  • Set observability standards — structured logging, tracing, Core Web Vitals and performance budgets, alerting — so the team can catch and resolve issues before Marketing does.

  • Lead how the team applies AI and ML to web workflows, from content operations to personalization to internal tooling, and act as the bridge between product engineering and web engineering.

  • Partner with Security and Infrastructure to harden the platform without slowing developer experience.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to a small, front-end-focused team through code review, design review, and architectural guidance.

 

What You Have

  • 8+ years of Web Development experience with deep back-end and systems expertise, and a track record of owning technical architecture at a staff level of scope and ambiguity.

  • Strong command of the modern web stack — React/Next.js, TypeScript, and server-side rendering — paired with genuine back-end depth (Node, Python, or comparable) rather than front-end specialization alone.

  • Experience architecting and operating headless CMS and content platforms (Sanity, Contentful, or similar) at scale, including schema design and publishing workflows.

  • Proven experience building and operating reliable production systems: CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, observability tooling, and performance optimization against real user metrics.

  • Fluency with data infrastructure fundamentals — SQL/NoSQL databases, caching, queuing, API and webhook integration patterns — in service of marketing and GTM systems.

  • Experience integrating AI/ML capabilities into production web experiences or content workflows.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor less experienced engineers, influence across functions, and operate autonomously in a small team where you are the deepest technical voice.

Nice to have: Vercel platform experience; marketing/GTM systems integration (HubSpot, Salesforce, Segment, analytics); SEO and web performance engineering; prior experience as the first or most senior engineer on a web platform team.

 

Compensation

$146,600 - $201,500 USD

 

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

We are looking for an experienced public sector lawyer to join our legal team to help build and lead Harvey’s government and public sector legal function. You will help drive our efforts to build relationships with, and sell to, government agencies. You will interface with our go-to-market, business and cross-functional teams (including Engineering, Product and Security) to help ensure the fast, efficient execution of our agreements with government customers and prime contractors.

 

What You'll Do

Generative AI has the power to greatly change the world and directly impact how things get done, including how governments and public sector agencies serve the public. Harvey is at the forefront of this change, and our mission is to make generative AI actionable and useful for our customers. This is a fast moving environment (we are a start-up!) that is serving some of the world’s most renowned law firms and professional organizations. And this role will put you in the center of all of this.

 

More specifically, you will:

  • Partner with cross-functional teams on potential opportunities and advise on public sector procurement processes, proposals, and strategies for selling Harvey’s platform to government agencies

  • Draft, review, and negotiate complex government contracts, AI SaaS agreements, and other technology-related agreements with federal, state, and local government customers and prime contractors, ensuring compliance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and agency-specific requirements

  • Provide contract lifecycle counsel across the public sector business, including contract administration, performance issues, and government contracting compliance obligations

  • Provide training and develop resources for legal and cross-functional teams

 

We are a small, but growing company, and one of the best things about working in such an environment is that there is lots of opportunity to pick up other aspects of the legal work that supports our company. While the principal job will be as described above, there will be ample opportunities to broaden your wheelhouse here at Harvey!

 

This role has flexibility to either be based in New York, N.Y.; San Francisco, CA; Chicago, IL; or Dallas, TX on a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office, or fully remote if based in another location within the US (DC preferred).

 

What You Have

  • A law degree from an accredited law school

  • Admitted to practice law and in good standing in at least one jurisdiction (California, New York, or DC preferred)

  • 7+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience

  • Transactional background, including with strong experience with complex SaaS, technology, and/or IP licensing and commercial agreements, with a particular focus on government contracts and public sector transactions

  • Experience negotiating complex agreements with federal, state, and/or local government customers and prime contractors

  • Working knowledge of government procurement regimes, including the FAR, DFARS, and related government contracting regulations and processes

  • Experience advising businesses on selling into the government and public sector, including go-to-market and procurement strategy

  • Ability to think creatively, function independently and work proactively in a fast-paced environment

  • Team-focused and collaborative work style; willingness to build expertise and solve new challenges in an evolving practice

  • Hyper-responsive and service-oriented attitude

  • Ninja-like project management skills

  • Bonus qualifications include prior government service, experience with AI, supporting Go-To-Market/ Sales, and a love for solving hard problems with a small tight-knit team.

 

Compensation

$210,300 - $300,000 USD

 

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

 

Role Overview

We are looking for an experienced public sector lawyer to join our legal team to help build and lead Harvey’s government and public sector legal function. You will help drive our efforts to build relationships with, and sell to, government agencies. You will interface with our go-to-market, business and cross-functional teams (including Engineering, Product and Security) to help ensure the fast, efficient execution of our agreements with government customers and prime contractors.

 

What You'll Do

Generative AI has the power to greatly change the world and directly impact how things get done, including how governments and public sector agencies serve the public. Harvey is at the forefront of this change, and our mission is to make generative AI actionable and useful for our customers. This is a fast moving environment (we are a start-up!) that is serving some of the world’s most renowned law firms and professional organizations. And this role will put you in the center of all of this.

 

More specifically, you will:

  • Partner with cross-functional teams on potential opportunities and advise on public sector procurement processes, proposals, and strategies for selling Harvey’s platform to government agencies

  • Draft, review, and negotiate complex government contracts, AI SaaS agreements, and other technology-related agreements with federal, state, and local government customers and prime contractors, ensuring compliance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and agency-specific requirements

  • Provide contract lifecycle counsel across the public sector business, including contract administration, performance issues, and government contracting compliance obligations

  • Provide training and develop resources for legal and cross-functional teams

 

We are a small, but growing company, and one of the best things about working in such an environment is that there is lots of opportunity to pick up other aspects of the legal work that supports our company. While the principal job will be as described above, there will be ample opportunities to broaden your wheelhouse here at Harvey!

 

This role has flexibility to either be based in New York, N.Y.; San Francisco, CA; Chicago, IL; or Dallas, TX on a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office, or fully remote if based in another location within the US (DC preferred).

 

What You Have

  • A law degree from an accredited law school

  • Admitted to practice law and in good standing in at least one jurisdiction (California, New York, or DC preferred)

  • 7+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience

  • Transactional background, including with strong experience with complex SaaS, technology, and/or IP licensing and commercial agreements, with a particular focus on government contracts and public sector transactions

  • Experience negotiating complex agreements with federal, state, and/or local government customers and prime contractors

  • Working knowledge of government procurement regimes, including the FAR, DFARS, and related government contracting regulations and processes

  • Experience advising businesses on selling into the government and public sector, including go-to-market and procurement strategy

  • Ability to think creatively, function independently and work proactively in a fast-paced environment

  • Team-focused and collaborative work style; willingness to build expertise and solve new challenges in an evolving practice

  • Hyper-responsive and service-oriented attitude

  • Ninja-like project management skills

  • Bonus qualifications include prior government service, experience with AI, supporting Go-To-Market/ Sales, and a love for solving hard problems with a small tight-knit team.

 

Compensation

$210,300 - $300,000 USD

jobs.title: Legal Operations Project Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Legal Operations Project Manager to join our legal team to help modernize how Legal operates through both best-in-class legal operations practices and hands-on use of AI. By combining traditional legal ops experience with familiarity with AI tools and automation platforms, you will help turn operational problems into scalable, AI-enabled solutions. You will partner closely with Legal and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver on the Legal Ops roadmap and help ensure that Legal’s tooling, data, and processes support Harvey’s rapid growth. It is a unique opportunity to be a key contributor to an AI-native legal operations function inside a company that is itself defining the future of AI for legal work.

What You'll Do

  • Manage end-to-end legal operations projects, including gathering requirements, designing and improving workflows, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders and managing implementation and iteration for areas such as intake, matter management, advice requests and policy changes

  • Translate priorities and direction into concrete project plans, timelines and execution steps, serving as the connective tissue between strategy and day-to-day delivery

  • Support AI enablement across Legal, including identifying use cases, evaluating and piloting AI tools (including Harvey), and helping with training and adoption efforts

  • Contribute to building and maintain legal metrics, dashboards and operational reporting across workload, turnaround times, risk patterns and operational performance

  • Support the evaluation, implementation, administration and continuous improvement of the legal technology stack and vendor relationships across knowledge management, matter tracking, e-billing and spend management, document management and contract-related tooling

  • Develop and maintain legal knowledge assets, including templates, playbooks, FAQs, self-service resources and internal documentation

  • Support routine operational, administrative, systems and data work as priorities evolve

What You Have

  • 3 to 6 years of experience in an operations or project management role, with responsibility for running and improving cross-functional systems, processes or programs; experience may come from legal operations, business operations, systems operations or a related function

  • Meaningful experience working in or closely with an in-house legal team, with a practical understanding of how Legal supports the business

  • A builder’s mindset: comfortable owning many moving pieces at once and energized by creating structure in a function that is still taking shape, rather than optimizing an established playbook

  • Experience contributing to the design and implementation of processes, systems and programs for Legal or other G&A functions, from requirements gathering through rollout and iteration

  • Comfortable working with both Legal and technical teams, helping turn business needs into practical process and system requirements, with experience or strong interest in applying AI tools in a legal or professional services setting

  • Comfortable operating with general guidance, seeking direction on new or unfamiliar issues, and balancing competing priorities and sustaining momentum in a globally distributed organization

  • Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with familiarity across legal technology (e.g. matter management, knowledge management, ticketing and document repositories) and experience building and interpreting metrics

Bonus Points

  • Hands-on experience with CLM or contracting systems

  • Practical experience building or deploying AI-driven workflows, with familiarity with agentic behavior, orchestration, prompt engineering, performance metrics and safety protocols

  • Experience helping design AI guidance, guardrails, or adoption programs for a legal or professional services team

Compensation

$99,200 - $148,800 USD

Role Overview

The Global Benefits and Leaves Analyst joins Harvey's Total Rewards team to support administering and improving employee benefits and leave programs across a rapidly scaling, global workforce. The team's mission is to deliver competitive, compliant, and employee-centric programs in every region where Harvey operates. This role manages day-to-day Tier 1 benefits support globally while partnering on benefits programs and vendor operations across EMEA and APAC, ensuring employees receive timely, accurate guidance and that programs run smoothly as Harvey expands into new markets. You’ll work closely with People Operations, Payroll, and external brokers, building operational rigor into a function that directly touches every employee. It is a chance to scale benefit operations at a category-defining AI company during a period of exceptional international growth.


What You'll Do

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for Tier 1 global benefits inquiries across all regions (including the US) with a responsive, service-oriented approach—resolving standard requests directly while escalating complex cases to the Benefits Program Managers.

  • Assist in administration and support of benefits programs and vendor relationships across EMEA and APAC, ensuring compliance with local regulations and alignment with Harvey's total rewards philosophy.

  • Coordinate leave-of-absence processes end-to-end — including statutory and company-provided leaves — across multiple jurisdictions.

  • Partner with Payroll and external brokers to ensure accurate benefits enrollment, changes, and offboarding workflows.

  • Analyze benefits utilization data and employee queries to identify trends and propose process improvements.

  • Partner with Benefit Program Managers on open enrollment execution, new-country benefit launches, and drafting employee communications.

  • Track, process, and reconcile benefits-related invoices from vendors and brokers.

  • Develop, maintain and update internal benefits documentation, employee FAQs, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) as programs scale.

  • Coordinate vendor onboarding, administrative PO creation, and contract workflows with guidance from Finance and Legal




What You Have

  • 2–4 years of experience in benefits administration, leave management, or a related HR operations role, ideally within a global or multi-country environment

  • Working knowledge of EMEA and/or APAC benefits structures, statutory requirements, and leave entitlements

  • Excellent communication and service orientation, with a track record of delivering responsive, empathetic employee support

  • Experience working with HRIS platforms (e.g., Workday), HR ticketing or case management systems (e.g., ServiceNow, Zendesk, Jira, or Workday Help), and benefits administration tools

  • Experience or exposure to benefits vendor/broker management

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret benefits data and produce actionable insights

  • Ability to manage day-to-day workflows independently while knowing when to seek guidance or escalate complex issues

  • Proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets (vlookups, pivot tables) for basic data analysis and invoice reconciliation

You'll establish the campaign operating model, prove what works, and build the team and capabilities to scale it globally.

This is a strategic player-coach role with meaningful influence across the company. You'll shape go-to-market priorities alongside leadership across marketing, product, GTM, and you'll stay close enough to the work to write the message, understand the data, and improve the campaign when it matters.

What You'll Do

  • Set Harvey's global integrated campaign strategy. Define the audiences, segments, narratives, and campaign architecture that build relevance with our audiences and drive awareness, engagement, pipeline, and revenue.

  • Turn audience insight into differentiated positioning. Develop messaging rooted in primary research, customer insight, competitive intelligence, and demonstrated use cases. Build claims on evidence and create narratives sophisticated audiences find credible.

  • Translate company priorities into market-facing programs. Partner with Product, Sales, and business leaders to develop marketing strategies around Harvey's most important growth initiatives, connecting what matters to the business with what matters to our audiences.

  • Orchestrate the full marketing system. Bring together digital, social, communications and analyst relations, alliances, events, field marketing, and other channels into cohesive global campaigns, spanning major launches, category-building moments, and always-on programs.

  • Build the measurement system. Define the KPIs, dashboards, attribution signals, and operating cadence that connect campaign investment to audience and business outcomes.

  • Build the team and operating model. Design how the campaigns function works, hire exceptional marketers, and develop them into strategic owners of audiences, programs, and business outcomes.

  • Raise the creative and strategic bar. Establish what great campaign thinking looks like at Harvey, from the quality of the insight and sharpness of the message to the craft of the execution and rigor of the measurement.

  • Build an AI-native campaign engine. Apply AI across audience research and modeling, creative development, experimentation, personalization, localization, and performance analysis. Develop repeatable approaches that raise the capabilities of the broader marketing organization.

What You Have

  • 8+ years of B2B marketing experience, including significant ownership of integrated campaigns, demand generation, or go-to-market programs within enterprise software or high-growth SaaS.

  • A record of building and scaling. You've created teams, programs, or operating models and know how to introduce structure without introducing unnecessary process.

  • Experience building and leading exceptional teams. You've hired, developed, and retained high-performing marketers.

  • Strong commercial instincts. You've owned multi-million-dollar investments and understand how to connect marketing decisions to audience impact, pipeline, revenue, and ROI.

  • Exceptional positioning and messaging judgment. You know how to get from audience research and market insight to a differentiated point of view, and you're a strong enough writer to do the work yourself when the stakes are high.

  • Exceptional cross-functional influence. You've orchestrated digital, social, communications, analyst relations, partnerships, events, and field marketing as one system rather than optimizing a single channel in isolation.

  • Hands-on fluency with AI. AI is already part of your campaign workflow. You have informed opinions about where it meaningfully improves marketing, and where human judgment remains the advantage.

  • A player-coach operating style. You're comfortable setting strategy with senior leaders and equally comfortable opening the doc, digging into the dashboard, rewriting the brief, or working through the details with the team.

  • Comfort with ambition and ambiguity. You can create clarity where there isn't yet a playbook, move quickly without lowering the bar, and build systems that become more sophisticated as Harvey grows.

Compensation

$164,000 - $246,000 USD

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

As a Product Operations Manager, Data at Harvey, you'll be the connective tissue between our data product surfaces, Engineering, GTM, and the external technology partners we rely on — making sure customer and partner signals turn into fast, well-coordinated action. You'll own intake and triage for feature requests and data issues, run early-access programs and cross-functional launches, and manage the partner relationships that keep our data pipeline reliable for law firms and in-house legal teams pushing the frontier of AI adoption.

This is a role for someone who's comfortable being in the weeds of a technical issue one hour and briefing leadership on launch risk the next — and who'd rather build a lightweight system that scales than a heavy process that doesn't get used.

What You'll Do

Customer, Partner & Issue Intake — Making sure the right signal reaches the right team, fast

  • Own the intake, triage, and prioritization of customer feature requests.

  • Triage customer-reported data and product issues, assess severity and impact, coordinate resolution across the appropriate teams, and ensure timely communication.

  • Manage relationships with external technology partners, including onboarding, ongoing operations, issue resolution, and delivery quality.

Programs & Launches — Getting new capabilities into customers' hands, then out the door broadly

  • Plan and run early-access programs for new features, including customer selection, onboarding, feedback collection, usage analysis, and launch recommendations.

  • Coordinate cross-functional launches by tracking dependencies, validating operational readiness, surfacing risks, and keeping high-priority initiatives on track.

Systems That Scale — Turning feedback and recurring friction into durable process

  • Translate customer, partner, and internal feedback into clear requirements, prioritized workstreams, and actionable recommendations.

  • Create and maintain documentation, playbooks, and enablement materials that help internal teams communicate and operate effectively.

  • Identify recurring operational challenges and implement lightweight systems, automation, and processes that enable the team to scale.

What You Have

  • 3-5+ years in Product Operations, Program Management, Technical Program Management, or a related operational role at a high-growth tech or SaaS company — ideally supporting data, integrations, or technical product surface.

  • Experience triaging and prioritizing inbound requests and issues at volume — you know how to separate signal from noise and route things to the right owner without becoming a bottleneck.

  • Comfortable engaging with data and technical issues directly enough to assess severity and impact, even when you're not the one fixing them.

  • Experience managing external vendor or technology partner relationships, including onboarding and ongoing delivery quality.

  • Hands-on experience running early-access or beta programs and coordinating launches in a fast-moving product environment.

The IT Operations Analyst joins Harvey's BizTech team to deliver seamless, high-touch technology support that keeps employees productive across a fast-moving AI company. The team's mission is to ensure every Harvey employee—from new hires to senior leadership—has frictionless access to the tools and systems they need to do their best work. This role drives day-to-day IT operations while contributing to automation, process improvement, and systems integration initiatives that scale support as the company grows. They partner closely with engineering, security, and cross-functional stakeholders to maintain reliable, secure infrastructure across Harvey's global offices. It is an opportunity to shape IT operations at a defining moment for legal AI—where initiative, technical curiosity, and a service-first mindset have outsized impact.

You’ll handle employee onboarding, lifecycle tasks, and aid employees with technology issues and workplace technology (A/V). This is a role ideal for someone with past experience in a fast-paced environment who is ready to make an impact.

What You'll Do

  • Create a great employee experience through hands-on IT support for employees in our New York City office.

  • Support onboarding and offboarding processes to ensure new hires are productive from day one and departures are handled cleanly and securely.

  • Provide white-glove IT support to employees across all levels, triaging requests via Slack, ticketing systems, and in-person interactions with a focus on speed and empathy.

  • Administer and optimize core SaaS platforms including Google Workspace, Okta, Slack, Zoom, and MDM solutions (Jamf/InTune) to ensure secure and reliable access.

  • Assist with meeting room tech and corporate events to ensure smooth hybrid meetings and high-quality A/V experiences.

  • Troubleshoot employee problems with applications, laptops, access, peripherals, printers, video conferencing, and networking issues.

  • Maintain IT asset inventory and coordinate hardware repairs, upgrades, and procurement.

  • Identify and resolve systemic issues through root cause analysis, escalating patterns to improve reliability across the technology stack.

  • Collaborate with the IT team on automation, documentation, and process improvements.

What You Have

  • 3+ years of experience in IT support experience in a fast-paced startup or tech environment.

  • Strong proficiency with identity and access management platforms (Okta preferred), Google Workspace administration, and macOS device management.

  • Experience with Google Workspace, Okta (SSO/MFA), Slack, and other SaaS tools.

  • Hands-on scripting or automation experience (e.g., Python, Bash, Okta Workflows) that goes beyond basic helpdesk troubleshooting.

  • Excellent communication and customer service skills with the ability to support senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders with patience and clarity.

  • A proactive, employee-first mindset—you notice problems before they're reported and take initiative to fix them.

  • Comfort working in a high-growth, ambiguous environment where priorities shift and resourcefulness is essential.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with scripting or automation (Python, Bash, PowerShell) to streamline IT tasks.

  • Experience managing MDM tools like Jamf, Kandji, or Intune.

  • Experience with Microsoft Office and Windows.

Compensation

$109,100 - $150,100 USD

jobs.title: GTM Enablement Manager, FLM Coaching
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Frontline managers are the most important lever in GTM performance. They set the coaching culture, run team reviews, and decide whether reps are actually developing or just executing. Right now, we don't have a dedicated person helping our managers get better at that work. This role builds that program — and owns it end to end.

The job is to build repeatable systems: a leader program that strengthens coaching habits and team effectiveness, a methodology reinforcement model that works in the flow of the quarter, and a new hire experience that gets NAMER reps ramped as fast as anyone. You define the vision, build the operating model, and track whether it's actually changing behavior.

What You'll Do

  • Manager coaching program — Build and own a structured program for frontline managers: what great looks like in a coaching conversation, a team review, a development plan. Make it repeatable with governance and success metrics that scale beyond you.

  • Methodology reinforcement — Translate our sales methodology into practical field behaviors and a reinforcement model that sticks long after the initial rollout.

  • Rep skills programs — Own foundational skill-building programs managers can't run alone: discovery, competitive positioning, core seller skills. Build the architecture, drive adoption, measure behavior change.

  • GTM process alignment — Partner with RevOps and Revenue Leadership to ensure coaching and training reinforce how we run the business.

  • Measurement — Define what success looks like (manager adoption, behavior change, field productivity) and use that signal to continuously improve. You're accountable for outcomes, not just delivery.

  • Manager Onboarding — Partner with our GTM Onboarding PM to develop best in class content and delivery for our newest managers.

What You Have

  • 6–8 years in enablement, learning & development, program management, or a related GTM role — ideally at a high-growth tech company

  • Proven track record building programs for frontline managers and leaders, not just individual contributors

  • Familiarity with a structured sales methodology (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or similar) and experience translating it into field behaviors and reinforcement

  • Strong program management instincts: governance, stakeholder rhythms, measurement frameworks — not just curriculum design

  • You understand what drives durable behavior change and build for that, not just completion rates

  • Ability to influence leaders and managers across functions without formal authority

  • Strong communicator who can bring clarity and structure to ambiguous, build-from-scratch work

Compensation

$136,000 - $187,000 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Role Overview

We are hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join the Solutions Marketing team to build the foundation for how Harvey's products show up as real, usable solutions for legal professionals. You'll set the standard for how Harvey packages, launches, and enables solutions across legal teams and emerging markets. Working closely with Marketing, Product, and GTM teams to define clear workflows, practical use cases, and repeatable, customer-ready assets across different segments and buyers. Success shows up as shared clarity across GTM, faster customer adoption and value realization, quality pipeline, and a durable story that scales as Harvey grows.

What You'll Do

  • Lead go-to-market strategy for a core solution area, translating product capabilities into messaging and positioning tailored to the vertical, persona, and segment size.

  • Enable GTM teams with solution-led messaging, demo storylines, playbooks, and customer-ready materials that support the enterprise sales motion.

  • Partner with Product and Core Product Marketing to shape launches and own how it gets packaged and adapted across target verticals and personas.

  • Partner with Demand Gen and Content to develop full funnel campaigns that build thought leadership, drive demand, and mature pipeline.

  • Regularly conduct market, customer, and competitive research, grounding positioning and strategy in real customer needs and differentiated value.

  • Align on solutions prioritization and market opportunity across Product, GTM, and Marketing leadership teams.

What You Have

  • 6-8+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Solutions Marketing, or a related role in B2B SaaS.

  • Proven experience marketing complex, workflow-driven products to enterprise buyers.

  • Demonstrated ability to connect technical product capabilities to customer problems, outcomes, and business value.

  • Expertise in developing positioning and messaging, and translating it into sales-facing and customer-facing assets across different audiences, segments, and verticals.

  • Experience contributing to product launches, including translating core launch messaging into content for specific industries or personas and building out assets.

Compensation

$137,600 - $206,400 USD

Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. You can find all of our Applicant Privacy Notices here.

Harvey is redefining what’s possible in legal work by combining cutting-edge AI with intuitive product experiences. As we scale rapidly and take on increasingly complex use cases, we’re expanding our product engineering team to accelerate our ability to ship fast, delight users, and build infrastructure that scales with us.

As a Senior Engineering Manager for Product Engineering, you’ll lead teams of backend engineers building the core product surfaces that lawyers and legal professionals use every day—from complex workflows and collaboration tools to elegant user interfaces powered by sophisticated backend systems. This role is equal parts product intuition and technical execution. You’ll be trusted to make fast, high-quality decisions, ship impactful features, and grow a team that embodies engineering excellence.

We move with urgency, bias toward simplicity, and expect our leaders to be hands-on when needed. If you’re energized by ownership, decisive execution, and solving real user problems, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

  • Lead engineers define, build, and drive the multi-quarter technical strategy for user-facing features across our product.

  • Collaborate closely with Design, Product, and AI teams to identify and execute on high-impact initiatives.

  • Help define and evolve the architecture for a fast-moving, AI-powered application.

  • Hire, grow, and retain exceptional engineers who thrive in a high-trust, high-impact environment.

  • Foster a culture of simplicity, quality, and continuous improvement.

  • Contribute to code and architecture reviews, unblock teams, and lead by example when needed.

  • Work closely with cross-functional partners to align product initiatives with company goals.

What You Have

  • 3+ years of experience in a software engineering management role leading product engineering teams, preferably in high-growth environments.

  • 12+ years of software engineering experience as a backend engineer.

  • A track record of leading high-performing, engaged engineering teams.

  • Strong product sense and an instinct for balancing speed, quality, and user impact.

  • Experience with backend systems (e.g., Python, Java, Go) and modern cloud-native infrastructure.

  • A plus: Exposure to AI-powered applications or complex internal tools.

  • Ability to anticipate scaling bottlenecks before they occur and take decisive, proactive measures.

  • Experience building RAG pipelines and managing the data lifecycle.

Additional Information

  • Work eligibility: Must be authorized to work in India. Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.
